evidence_span.text: The antibodies against CMG-1 allowed us to detect primary cilia in cultured human umbilical vein endothelial cells (HUVEC) and find conditions eliciting the disassembly of these cilia.

reviews.rationale: The paper directly demonstrates primary cilia and a putative IFT component in human endothelial cells, supporting the endothelial-context rationale. Its IFT-71/IFT74 experiments do not establish the assigned Ift74-dependent tubulin-transport function.

evidence_span.text: For Opa1, Chchd3, Mitofilin, and Chchd6 knockouts, the number of cristae per mitochondrion decreased, as did the cristae score and cristae surface area compared with the WT (Figure 4i–k).

reviews.rationale: Chchd6 knockout in primary mouse myotubes causally reduced multiple cristae measures, supporting its role in MICOS-dependent inner-membrane organization. The experiment is ex vivo skeletal muscle rather than an in vivo knockout or brain endothelium.

evidence_span.text: These findings indicate that one of the major functions of Cep164 in ciliogenesis is to recruit active TTBK2 to centrioles.

reviews.rationale: Loss, interaction, and rescue experiments support Cep164 recruitment of TTBK2 as a trigger for ciliogenesis. The cached abstract does not identify the organism or cell type, preventing context calibration.

evidence_span.text: Once at the base of the cilium, NINL interacts with CC2D2A, providing the specificity of the docking point at the entrance to the ciliary compartment.

reviews.rationale: Gene-specific interaction, localization, and mutant evidence supports CC2D2A as a ciliary-base docking component in RAB8-linked vesicle trafficking. The retinal and cultured-cell systems are indirect to postnatal mouse brain endothelium.
